messages:
tess_rust: hit a nasty pattern in the rust sampleapp today: force token rotate and prefetch=5 produced a big synchronized retry -> many 429s. anyone else?
omar_qe: can you share the minimal repro? sounds like mutex + prefetch amplification.
tess_rust: run sampleapp with concurrency=20, prefetch=5, then rotate key. sequence: many 401s, refresh starts, then refresh completes and all workers retry instantly. log: 
```
[2026-04-01T07:22:10Z] req=10 status=401
[2026-04-01T07:22:10Z] refresh:start
[2026-04-01T07:22:15Z] refresh:done
[2026-04-01T07:22:15Z] burst retries -> 429 x 80
```
sam_sdk: quick read: rust client holds a global async lock for refresh so inflight tasks block; when lock releases they all hit resend. go/js use a single-winner future so others await the in-progress refresh without re-triggering. also looks like per-request backoff state gets reset on refresh, which makes it worse.
lucy_docs: sampleapp prefetcher spawns page fetches immediately when slots free; that behavior is fine normally but amplifies head-of-line lock releases. we should change sampleapp defaults and add guidance.
mike_infra: impact: if many customers have similar clients, simultaneous token rotation could induce platform-wide throttle spikes. propose fixes: narrow lock scope; winner refresh future; preserve per-request backoff across refresh; add jittered retry for prefetcher; respect Retry-After.
omar_qe: i'll add a CI stress test that simulates N clients expiring at the same time and asserts tail spike < 1.5x baseline.
sam_sdk: i'll open a rust PR with: (1) fast-path expiry check outside lock, (2) winner-only HTTP refresh under lock, (3) per-request backoff preserved, (4) sampleapp default prefetch=2 and jitter 30-150ms.
ci-bot: CI: created branch rust-refresh-fix and PR #4999 (draft) for review.
lucy_docs: i'll add a "safe prefetch" note to quickstart and sampleapp README; include a diag flag to simulate token expiry locally.
tess_rust: thanks, please also add a short migration note for users upgrading rust sdk.
